subject: Post-demo: stream replay test window & access checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@streamlytics.com>; Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@streamlytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Apr 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: stream replay test window & access checklist

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps to get the customer-led traffic replay (streaming concurrency) scheduled:

1) Acceptance targets:
- 95th pct latency <= 220ms for single-shot generation (non-streaming)
- Streaming tail latency: final token arrival <= 350ms 95th
- Sustained throughput: 400 concurrent streams with average 30 tokens/sec per stream

2) Test artifacts we need from your side (I've attached placeholders):
- traffic_matrix.csv (sample distribution of session lengths / token rates) [Attachment: traffic_matrix.csv (CSV)]
- Any k6/Locust scripts you plan to run or a pointer to your repo. We can run your k6 script as-is or adapt our replay harness.
- IP ranges to allowlist for the test agents: please confirm NAT/egress IPs.

3) Access + accounts:
- We will provision two test API keys with rate-limited quota for the rehearsal. Please confirm which email addresses to tie them to.
- For streaming tests, we recommend client-side backpressure (if applicable) and a max-connection-per-IP limit so we don’t trip infra protections.

4) Proposed test window: Tue Apr 15, 09:00–11:00 PT (2 hour dry-run) with a follow-up 60-minute peak run at 11:30.

Ben and Soojin are looped for runtime orchestration and script validation. If this looks good I’ll prepare an ops runbook and push the test keys.

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: k6_replay_script.js (placeholder)]

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick answers:
- Acceptance targets: agreed on the non-streaming latency. For streaming tail we can accept <= 380ms 95th for the first run and tighten if the dry-run looks good.
- We'll attach our traffic_matrix.csv and a cleaned k6 replay script tonight.
- IP ranges: we run the replay from our CI runners (aws-us-east-2). Current egress IP list is attached.

Please provision the test keys to alicia.gomez@streamlytics.com and tom.reynolds@streamlytics.com. We’ll have two engineers (Raj and Priya) on the call for the dry-run.

Tom — can you confirm CI egress IPs?

Best,
Alicia

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@streamlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, eng-team@streamlytics.com
Date: Sat, 12 Apr 2025 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo: stream replay test window & access checklist

Thanks Alicia — I validated the allowlist file and added a few recommended CIDR entries for our test agents. Small ops notes from the infra side:
- We’ll create two keys: replay-read and replay-eval. The read key has lower token throughput and will be useful for latency-only probes. The eval key will be rate-limited to the planned concurrency profile.
- For streaming tests we’ll enable per-connection metrics (open, close, bytes_sent) and a token-level latency trace. Please make sure your k6 script emits the X-Request-ID header for correlating traces.
- If your CI runs behind changing NAT IPs, give us the runner pool tag (we can add a CIDR block range that covers it) — otherwise use the static egress list you sent.

I attached a minimal adaptation of your k6 script (k6_replay_script.js) with an example header injection and a traffic ramp schedule. We’ll push the runbook link to the shared drive once Marissa confirms the window.

—Ben
SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: k6_replay_script.js (JS)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Post-demo: stream replay test window & access checklist

Alicia / Tom —

All set on our end. Keys provisioned and emailed to the addresses requested (replay-read + replay-eval). Ben and Soojin will start the dry-run at 09:00 PT and I’ll be on the call at 09:10 to do a brief SLA acceptance check. Agenda for the dry-run:
- 09:00–09:20: verify connectivity, headers, and allowlist (smoke)
- 09:20–09:50: ramp to 50% concurrency profile (observe tail latency)
- 09:50–11:00: full run at target concurrency with traces enabled
- 11:30: 60-minute focused peak run if dry-run stable

If you see any 5xxs please post to the shared drive runbook and we’ll triage on the call. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-streamlytics-replay

See you shortly —
Marissa
